claims.evidence: No label, tag, or stamped code is legible in any photo; M272 is actually a Mercedes-Benz V6 engine code, not a transmission model, so this claim cannot be matched to the part shown.
No import paperwork, country-of-origin sticker, or shipping documentation is visible; background shows bare dirt ground typical of a local yard, not import packaging.
No video, audio clip, or bench-test rig is shown; the unit is static and disassembled in the photos, which cannot demonstrate operation or noise.
No odometer, vehicle history, or donor-vehicle photo is provided to link mileage to this specific unit.
Photo 2 shows the bellhousing separated from the torque converter with chalk-circle and red marker inspection marks, indicating the unit has been taken apart and marked, not left sealed/never opened.

risks.risk: Torque converter leaks or is out of balance
risks.proof: A bench spin-test video or pressure/leak-test clip of the converter alone
risks.if_unproven: priced as a converter of unknown integrity (worst case: needs replacement/rebuild)

risks.risk: Internal gear, clutch, and seal wear not visible from outside
risks.proof: Photos/video of the internal gear train and clutch packs with the case opened, or a documented teardown report
risks.if_unproven: priced as condition-unknown internals, assume rebuild needed

risks.proof: Photo of dipstick/fill plug with fluid level and color shown

risks.risk: Incomplete sensor/solenoid set or wiring harness damage
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all connector pins and a continuity test clip
risks.if_unproven: priced as incomplete electronics, assume some sensors missing or faulty

risks.risk: Vehicle/engine compatibility unconfirmed (model claim conflicts with engine code naming)
risks.proof: A clear photo of the stamped transmission ID/part number plate
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified fitment, buyer bears compatibility risk

risks.risk: Unit was opened/inspected, possibly for a prior fault, contradicting 'never opened' claim
risks.proof: Seller explanation plus close-up of the chalk/marker marks and any reassembly gasket evidence
risks.if_unproven: priced as a previously serviced/opened unit, not factory-sealed

risks.risk: No warranty or return policy stated
risks.if_unproven: priced as a final-sale, no-recourse item

proof_requests: Clear photo of the transmission's stamped ID/part number plate
Video of the unit running or at least the torque converter spinning without noise
Photo of fluid level/color via dipstick or fill plug
Close-up of all sensor/solenoid connectors and harness condition
Any import/customs documentation supporting the Belgium origin claim
Explanation and photos clarifying why the torque converter and bellhousing are shown separated with inspection marks
response.reason: The witness confirms this is an automatic transmission assembly with torque converter, so it can be priced at worst case; several seller claims are unverifiable and the 'never opened' claim is directly contradicted by visible disassembly and inspection marks.
